mainTopic: Witnesses serving as judges (עד נעשה דיין) and how a court of three ratifies a שטר
overview: The amud opens with a short story. רבנאי quotes שמואל saying that a witness and a judge can join together. אמימר praises the ruling, but רב אשי answers that רבא already refuted it. Next comes a ruling of רב about three judges ratifying a שטר when only two of them recognize the signatures: the two may testify before the third so he can sign with them. A challenge from רבא's rule, that a ratification written too early 'looks like a lie', leads the גמרא to correct the deadline from 'before they signed' to 'before they wrote'. The גמרא draws three lessons from this ruling, but רב אשי shows that only one holds up: עד נעשה דיין, a witness can become a judge. רב ספרא challenges that lesson from the new-moon משנה, and רב answers that עדות החודש is Torah law and stricter, while קיום שטרות is only rabbinic. Finally, רב rules on a judge whose fitness is challenged, and the גמרא begins asking what kind of challenge is meant. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבנאי reports a ruling of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבנאי, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא, came to town to sell sesame and quoted שמואל: a witness and a judge can join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנאי, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא, happened to come to sell sesame. He said: This is what שמואל said: a witness and a judge join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story in which a visitor passes on a ruling in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is that a person who acts as a witness and a person who acts as a judge can be combined in this kind of case. This ties back to the earlier discussion on the דף about judges who also know the signatures. The next steps react to this ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַע רַבְנַאי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Ravnai, the brother of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, happened to come
to sell sesame,
and he said: This is what Shmuel said:
A witness and a judge join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by reporting a ruling that ties back to the earlier discussion on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the report in שמואל's name, a witness and a judge can combine.

steps.title: אמימר praises the ruling
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says this ruling is excellent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: How excellent this teaching is!
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר voices strong approval of the ruling רבנאי reported. This sets up רב אשי's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר is not adding a new argument. He is endorsing the ruling, which gives רב אשי something to react to.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
How excellent is this teaching!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַמֵּימָר: כַּמָּה מְעַלְּיָא הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Endorses the ruling reported in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר approves of the ruling that a witness and a judge combine.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the praise: רבא already refuted it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells אמימר that he only praises the ruling because his mother's father praised it, and that רבא already disproved it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: Just because your mother's father praised it, you praise it too? רבא already refuted it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back hard on אמימר. The ruling should not be praised, because רבא already showed it is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי suggests that אמימר's praise comes from family loyalty to his grandfather, not from the strength of the argument. He then points to an earlier refutation by רבא, so the ruling 'a witness and a judge combine' is rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling 'a witness and a judge join together' is rejected. רבא already refuted it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
Because your mother's father praised it,
phrases.notes: This is רמי בר חמא, אמימר's grandfather, who had praised this very ruling.

phrases.english: you also praise it?!
Rava already refuted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אמימר's praise and the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ruling that a witness and a judge combine, and אמימר's praise of it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא had already shown the ruling to be incorrect. The praise came from loyalty to a grandfather, not from a strong argument.

steps.title: רב: two judges may testify before the third, but only before they sign
steps.stepSummary: Three judges are ratifying a שטר and only two recognize the signatures. The two may testify before the third so he can sign with them, but only if they have not signed yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three judges sat to ratify a document. Two recognize the witnesses' signatures and one does not. Before the two have signed, they may testify before him and he signs. Once they have signed, they may not testify before him and have him sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling of רב, passed down through a long chain of teachers, about how a בית דין of three ratifies a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two judges who know the signatures can act as witnesses for the third judge, so all three end up verifying the שטר. The timing matters. Once the two have already signed the ratification, it is too late, because when they signed there was not yet a full court of three that had verified the signatures.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (another version of who said it)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the two judges are not testifying in a regular court case. They are telling their fellow judge that the signatures are real, so he can join in the ratification.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rav Safra said that Rabbi Abba said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: that Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said
that Rav Huna said;

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Three who sat to ratify a document,
phrases.notes: The 'three' are three judges forming a court.

phrases.english: two recognize the signatures of the witnesses,
and one does not recognize them.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָתְמוּ — מְעִידִין בְּפָנָיו וְחוֹתֵם.
phrases.english: As long as they have not signed, they testify before him and he signs.
Once they have signed, they do not testify before him and have him sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling about three judges ratifying a שטר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two judges who know the signatures may testify to the third so he can sign, but only before they themselves have signed.

steps.title: Challenge: writing the ratification early looks like a lie
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ratification could be written before all three judges verified the signatures. רבא ruled that a ratification written before the signatures were verified is invalid because it looks like a lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really write the ratification first? But רב פפי said in the name of רבא: a judges' ratification written before the witnesses testified about their signatures is invalid, because it looks like a lie. Here too it looks like a lie!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling. His wording suggests the two judges wrote the ratification before the third judge knew the signatures, and that seems to break a rule of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule is that the ratification may not be written before the signatures are confirmed, because it claims something not yet true. If the two judges wrote it before the third judge had verified the signatures, the document claims a full court verified it when that had not happened yet. So it should be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: the judges' ratification (the court's statement confirming the document)

phrases.english: And do we write?
phrases.notes: He means: do we write the ratification before all the judges have verified the signatures?

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Pappi say in the name of Rava:
This ratification of judges

phrases.aramaic: דְּנִיכְתַּב מִקַּמֵּיהּ דְּנַיחְווֹ סָהֲדִי אַחֲתִימַת יְדַיְיהוּ —
phrases.english: that was written before the witnesses testified about their signatures —
is invalid, because it looks like a lie,
here too it looks like a lie!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי כָּתְבִינַן? וְהָאָמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב's ruling from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication in step 4 that the ratification is written before the third judge has verified the signatures.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא ruled that a ratification written before the signatures are verified is invalid because it looks like a lie. רב's case seems to involve exactly that.

steps.title: Correct the wording: 'before they wrote' instead of 'before they signed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects רב's ruling. The deadline is not signing but writing: before the ratification is written, the two may testify before the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: As long as they have not written it, they testify before him and he signs. Once they have written it, they do not testify before him and have him sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing one word in רב's ruling, from 'signed' to 'wrote.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the corrected wording, the ratification is never written before all three judges know the signatures are real, so nothing 'looks like a lie.' The two testify first, then the ratification is written and all three sign. Once the ratification has already been written, it is too late, because רבא's rule makes it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: as long as they have not written

steps.whatToRemember: The two judges who know the signatures may testify before the third, but only before the ratification is written. Once it is written, it is too late, because a ratification written before the signatures were verified looks like a lie.

phrases.english: Rather, say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא כָּתְבוּ — מְעִידִין בְּפָנָיו וְחוֹתֵם,
phrases.english: As long as they have not written, they testify before him and he signs,
once they have written, they do not testify before him and have him sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by correcting the wording of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the original ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling seemed to allow the ratification to be written before the third judge verified the signatures, with only the signing as the deadline.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real deadline is writing the ratification. The two testify before it is written, so it never looks like a lie.

steps.title: Three lessons learned from the ruling
steps.stepSummary: From the ruling about the two judges testifying before the third, the גמרא learns three rules: a witness can become a judge; judges who recognize the signatures do not need testimony; judges who do not recognize them need testimony before each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn three things from this. First, a witness can become a judge. Second, judges who recognize the witnesses' signatures do not need anyone to testify before them. Third, judges who do not recognize the signatures need testimony before each and every one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls three practical rules out of the ruling it just finished fixing in Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two judges testified about the signatures and then signed as judges, so a witness can become a judge. They did not need anyone to testify to them because they already knew the signatures. The third judge needed testimony, so every judge who does not recognize the signatures needs it personally.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. Introduces a conclusion drawn from a source.
A witness can become a judge in the same case.
The handwritten signatures of the witnesses on a שטר.
To testify before them, here meaning before the judges.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this.
phrases.notes: "This" is the corrected ruling from Step 6, where two judges testify before the third.

phrases.english: Learn from it: a witness can become a judge,
and learn from it: judges who recognize
the signatures of the witnesses
do not need anyone to testify before them,
and learn from it: judges who do not recognize
the signatures of the witnesses

phrases.aramaic: צְרִיכִין לְהָעִיד בִּפְנֵי כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: need testimony before each and every one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws practical rules from the ruling as corrected in Step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three rules: עד נעשה דיין; judges who recognize the signatures need no testimony; judges who do not recognize them need testimony before each one.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the second lesson
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי agrees we learn עד נעשה דיין. But maybe judges who recognize the signatures really do need testimony, and here it was enough because some testimony was given before one judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this. Fine, we can learn that a witness can become a judge. But how can we learn that judges who recognize the signatures do not need testimony? Maybe they really do need it, and this case is different because testimony was given before one of the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי accepts the first lesson but pushes back on the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There may be a basic rule that some testimony must be given in court before a שטר can be ratified. In our case that rule was met when the two testified before the third judge. So the case does not prove that judges who know the signatures need no testimony at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different. This case is special.
The act of giving testimony before the court.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say judges definitely need testimony. He only says the case cannot prove they don't.

phrases.english: רב אשי challenged this:
Granted, that a witness can become a judge
we do learn from it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דַּיָּינִין הַמַּכִּירִין חֲתִימוּת יְדֵי עֵדִים
phrases.english: but that judges who recognize the signatures of witnesses
do not need testimony before them?
Perhaps I can tell you that they really do need it,
and here it is different
because the requirement of testimony is met with one.
phrases.notes: "One" means the third judge. The two testified before him, so some testimony did happen in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second lesson drawn in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the second lesson. The first lesson, עד נעשה דיין, is accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case had some testimony before one judge, so it cannot prove that no testimony is needed at all.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the third lesson
steps.stepSummary: Maybe judges who do not recognize the signatures do not need testimony before each one. Here it was needed only because otherwise there would have been no testimony at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how can we learn that judges who do not recognize the signatures need testimony before each one? Maybe they really don't need it, and this case is different because without it there would be no testimony at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי continues and rejects the third lesson the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case, if the two had not testified before the third judge, no testimony would have been given in court at all. That is why it was needed here. When other testimony exists, maybe a judge could rely on what was said before his colleagues.
steps.whatToRemember: Only the lesson עד נעשה דיין survives from this case. The two rules about testifying before judges cannot be proven from it.

phrases.aramaic: וְדַיָּינִין שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין חֲתִימוּת יְדֵי עֵדִים
phrases.english: And that judges who do not recognize the signatures of witnesses

phrases.aramaic: צְרִיכִין לְהָעִיד בִּפְנֵי כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: need testimony before each and every one?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ: אֵין צְרִיכִין,
phrases.english: Perhaps I can tell you that they really do not need it,
and here it is different
because otherwise the requirement of testimony would not be met at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַיָּינִין שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין חֲתִימוּת יְדֵי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's challenge, now against the third lesson.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Testimony was needed here only because there was no other testimony at all, so the case proves nothing general.

steps.title: רבי אבא teaches that a witness can become a judge
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא sat and taught the rule עד נעשה דיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא sat and taught this teaching that a witness can become a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move. רבי אבא teaches עד נעשה דיין, and the next step challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עד נעשה דיין is the one lesson that survived רב אשי's challenge. Now someone teaches it publicly, which opens the door for a new objection.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat. Usually describes a teacher giving a lesson.
And he was saying, or teaching.

phrases.english: רבי אבא sat and taught
this teaching that a witness can become a judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the lesson that survived Steps 8 and 9 and presents it as a taught ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עד נעשה דיין: a witness can become a judge.

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges from the new-moon משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא quotes a משנה: if three judges saw the new moon, two must step down and testify before a new court of three. If a witness could become a judge, why not let all three stay seated and sanctify the month?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא challenged רבי אבא from a משנה: If three people saw the new moon and they are a court, two of them stand up and seat two of their colleagues next to the one who remains. They testify before them, and the judges say, "The month is sanctified, sanctified!" This is because one person alone is not trusted to do it. Now if a witness can become a judge, why all this? Let them stay in their places and sanctify the month!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks עד נעשה דיין with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the two judges who saw the moon do not remain judges. They step down, testify, and are replaced. That suggests a witness cannot become a judge. If he could, the original three could simply have sanctified the month themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: "The month is sanctified." The court's declaration of a new month.
A single person or a lone judge.
If it enters your mind, meaning if you really think so.
Why do I need all this?

steps.confusionAlert: The two who testify do not leave entirely. They are replaced as judges so a fresh court of three hears their testimony.

phrases.english: רב ספרא challenged רבי אבא:
If three people saw it, and they are a court,
phrases.notes: "It" is the new moon. This is a משנה in ראש השנה 25b.

phrases.english: two of them stand up and seat some of their colleagues
next to the one who remains,
and they testify before them,
and the judges say: "The month is sanctified, sanctified."

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הַיָּחִיד נֶאֱמָן עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: For a single person is not trusted on his own.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּעֵד נַעֲשֶׂה דַּיָּין,
phrases.english: And if you think that a witness can become a judge,
why do I need all this?
Let them stay seated in their places and sanctify the month!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule רבי אבא taught in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's rule of עד נעשה דיין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the witnesses step down and be replaced as judges. That would be pointless if a witness could also serve as a judge.

steps.title: Torah law is stricter than rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says he had the same question. It went up a chain of teachers all the way to רב, who answered that עדות החודש is a Torah law and קיום שטרות is rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I had the same difficulty. I asked רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, he asked רב הונא, רב הונא asked חייא בר רב, and חייא בר רב asked רב. רב told them: Don't compare testimony about the new month, which is a Torah law, to ratifying documents, which is a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers רב ספרא's question from the new moon משנה. The new moon case is a Torah law with stricter rules, so it cannot disprove עד נעשה דיין for documents, which is only a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא argued that if a witness could become a judge, the judges who saw the moon should not need to step down and could simply stay seated. רב's answer is that עדות החודש comes from the Torah, so there we are strict and a witness may not judge. קיום שטרות is only rabbinic, so the חכמים allowed a witness to act as a judge.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that the new moon was seen, so the new month can be declared
Ratifying documents: a court confirms the witnesses' signatures are real

steps.whatToRemember: עד נעשה דיין still works for קיום שטרות, because that is rabbinic. The new moon case is stricter because it is a Torah law.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the new moon משנה is wrong. He is saying it is a separate, stricter case, so it cannot disprove the rule for documents.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: It was difficult for me as well,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אבא, answering רב ספרא's question from step 11.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁאֵילְתֵּיהּ לְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא,
phrases.english: and I asked it of Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta,
and Rav Yitzchak asked Rav Huna,
and Rav Huna asked Chiyya bar Rav,
and Chiyya bar Rav asked Rav,
and he said to them:
Leave aside testimony about the new month, which is from the Torah,
while ratifying documents is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the new moon משנה in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: Torah law against rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The new moon משנה shows that a witness can never become a judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strictness applies only to Torah-level עדות החודש. For rabbinic קיום שטרות, a witness may become a judge.

steps.title: A challenged judge on a court ratifying a document
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if one of three judges ratifying a document is challenged, the other two may testify that he is fit only before they sign, not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: Three judges sat to ratify a document, and someone challenged one of them. If they have not signed yet, the other two testify about him and he signs. Once they have signed, they do not testify about him so that he can sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב about a court of three ratifying a document when one judge's fitness is challenged. Timing decides whether the other two may vouch for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before signing, the two other judges can act as witnesses that the third judge is fit, and then he joins in signing. After they have signed, they may no longer vouch for him. The common explanation is that by then they look like they are protecting their own signatures.

keyTerms.meaning: To ratify or confirm a document
A challenge or protest against someone's fitness

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling also fits עד נעשה דיין. The two judges serve as witnesses about the third and still stay on as his fellow judges.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Three who sat to ratify the document,
and someone raised a challenge against one of them.
Before they have signed,
they testify about him, and he signs.
phrases.notes: "They" are the other two judges, who vouch that the challenged judge is fit.

phrases.english: Once they have signed,
they do not testify about him so that he can sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עד נעשה דיין discussion closes, a new ruling of רב about ratifying documents is introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before signing, the other two judges may testify that a challenged judge is fit, and he then signs. After they have signed, they may not.

steps.title: What kind of challenge is meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of challenge רב was talking about and begins with the possibility that the judge was accused of being a robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of challenge? If it was a challenge that he is a robber...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of challenge against the judge רב had in mind. It starts testing the first possibility, an accusation of robbery. This is a setup line, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different challenges have different results. A robber is disqualified from judging, but other challenges, such as a problem with family lineage, may work differently. The גמרא is going to test each option to see which one fits רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbery, being a robber, which disqualifies a person

phrases.english: A challenge of what kind?
If it was a challenge that he is a robber,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where the גמרא shows the problem with this option.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what kind of challenge is meant in רב's ruling from step 13.
